entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-26w4-8w32-4x3v: Slack Morphism verifier errors disclose valid HMACs in the logs
entry.content:
Slack Morphism verifier errors disclose valid HMACs in the logs

Aliases: CVE-2026-113799

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • slack-morphism — fixed in 2.28.0

### Summary Slack Morphism exposes the correct Slack request HMAC when signature verification fails. For an invalid request, `slack-morphism` computes the correct signature for the attacker-controlled timestamp and request body and stores it in `SlackEventWrongSignatureError.generated_hash`. The error's `Debug` and `Display` representations expose that value, and the default Axum listener error handler logs it at error level. An attacker who can both reach the application's Slack callback endpoint and read its application/service logs can therefore use the verifier as a chosen-message HMAC oracle. The attacker can send an arbitrary request with an invalid signature, recover the correct signature from the resulting log entry, and resend the same request within the five-minute freshness w…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4gg8-gxpx-9rph: uv is vulnerable to arbitrary file write through entry point names
entry.content:
uv is vulnerable to arbitrary file write through entry point names

Aliases: CVE-2026-114109

Affected:

  • uv — fixed in 0.11.15
  • uv — fixed in 0.11.15

### Impact In versions of uv prior to 0.11.15, when installing a distribution containing an entry point specification (under `console_scripts` or `gui_scripts`), uv would place the generated entry point according to the given name even if doing so resulted in a path outside of the environment's scripts directory. A malicious wheel could use this to place an executable outside of the intended environment, including in a directory already present on the user's `PATH`. This could shadow or overwrite an existing executable and potentially result in unexpected code execution under the wheel's control, even if the wheel's installation environment was not explicitly added to `PATH` by the user. In order to exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must induce their target into installing a mali…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0381: Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates
entry.content:
Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates

Aliases: CVE-2026-111943, GO-2026-6809, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383

Affected:

  • webpki-roots — fixed in 0.26.11, 1.0.10

Affected versions include `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, which can allow certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates. Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign intermediate public keys. The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known. Version 1.0.10+ removes this root. The `webpki-roots` 0.26.11 compatibility package contains no independent trust store and re-exports the roots from its separately resolved 1.x dependency. That parent dependency must resolve to 1.0.10 or newer; an older parent remains affected by this advisory.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/webpki-roots

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0383: Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates
entry.content:
Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates

Aliases: CVE-2026-111943, GO-2026-6809, RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382

Affected:

  • webpki-root-certs — fixed in 0.26.11, 1.0.10

Affected versions include `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, which can allow certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates. Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign intermediate public keys. The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known. Version 1.0.10+ removes this root. Version 0.26.11 is a compatibility wrapper that re-exports `parent::TLS_SERVER_ROOT_CERTS` from its `webpki-root-certs` 1.x dependency; it contains no separate root certificate list. Its resolved 1.x dependency must be updated to 1.0.10 or later.

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0382: Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates
entry.content:
Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates

Aliases: CVE-2026-111943, GO-2026-6809, RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0383

Affected:

  • rustls-webpki — fixed in 0.103.16, 0.104.0-alpha.8

Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign intermediate public keys when the configured trust anchors allow such paths. entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0262: `append-only-vec` 0.1.9 was removed from crates.io due to a malicious dependency
entry.content:
`append-only-vec` 0.1.9 was removed from crates.io due to a malicious dependency

Affected:

  • append-only-vec — fixed in 0.1.10-0

A new version of the `append-only-vec` crate was published with a direct dependency on `proc-macro1`, which would execute a malicious build script. The compromised version of this crate was published on 2026-08-20, and was removed approximately 107 minutes later. The compromised crate version was used as part of a malware campaign targeted at users of `arrayref`, which was downloaded 2,285 times before being removed; see [the `arrayref` advisory][arrayref-advisory] for more detail. [arrayref-advisory]: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0260.html

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j7h2-66j4-ghjf: A russh SSH server accepts a publickey authentication whose signature uses a different algorithm than the one named in the request
entry.content:
A russh SSH server accepts a publickey authentication whose signature uses a different algorithm than the one named in the request

Aliases: CVE-2026-111062

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • russh — fixed in 0.64.0

### Details In `russh/src/server/encrypted.rs`, `server_read_auth_request_pk` (0.63.3, around lines 880-990): * The requested algorithm name (`pubkey_algo`) is read and only used to decode the key: `PublicKeyOrCertificate::decode(&pubkey_algo, &pubkey_key)`. The derived `hash_alg` is then dropped (`PublicKeyOrCertificate::PublicKey { ref key, .. }`). * The signature blob is decoded (`Signature::decode`) and verified with `Verifier::verify(&pubkey, &buf, &sig)`. `ssh-key` picks the hash from **the signature's own algorithm** (`sig.algorithm()`). * `pubkey_algo` and `sig.algorithm()` are never compared. So for an RSA key, the request can say `rsa-sha2-512` while the signature is `ssh-rsa`. The signature is valid for SHA-1, verification succeeds, and `Handler::auth_publickey` is called. *…

  • https://github.com/Eugeny/russh/security/advisories/GHSA-j7h2-66j4-ghjf

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4wc5-f2rc-q74m: russh: Unbounded memory allocation in agent protocol server via crafted constraint records
entry.content:
russh: Unbounded memory allocation in agent protocol server via crafted constraint records

Aliases: CVE-2026-111061

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • russh — fixed in 0.64.1

### Summary `russh_keys::agent::server::add_key` (`russh/src/keys/agent/server.rs:271-319`) spawns a dedicated tokio task for every 5-byte `SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_LIFETIME` record attached to an added key, each cloning the key blob and sleeping for the declared lifetime (up to ~136 years). The loop has no per-request task budget, and spawned tasks are not rolled back when the overall request fails. Repeating one constrained add-key message over an agent connection converts wire bytes into resident tasks and heap at roughly 141x amplification: in our measurement 10.2 MiB of protocol traffic produced ~2,096,120 live tasks and +1,447,856 KiB RSS, while the same traffic sent as unconstrained add-key requests cost +268 KiB. An attacker reaching the agent socket (a local process, or a remote SSH s…
